ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حم (١) وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ (٢)).
His saying (وَالْكِتَابِ): whoever makes «حم» an oath takes the wāw as a conjunction; and whoever says otherwise makes it the wāw of the oath.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِمَا ضَرَبَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ مَثَلًا ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ (١٧)).
His saying (وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا): the noun of ظَلَّ and its khabar (predicate). It is also possible that the noun of «ظَلَّ» is a latent pronoun (mustatir) referring to أَحَدُهُمْ, with وَجْهُهُ a badal (substitute) of it. Both are also read in the nominative (وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدٌّ), as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the khabar of ظَلَّ. (وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the noun of «ظَلَّ», or of the pronoun in «مُسْوَدًّا».
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَمَنْ يُنَشَّأُ فِي الْحِلْيَةِ وَهُوَ فِي الْخِصَامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ (١٨)).
His saying (أَوَمَنْ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative, its implied wording being "do you then make one who is brought up…"; or in the position of the nominative, i.e. "is one who is brought up… a part [of Him] or a child?". And (فِي الْخِصَامِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مُبِينٍ». If you say: the muḍāf ilayhi (second term of a genitive construct) does not govern what precedes it?
It is answered: except with «غَيْرُ», because it contains the meaning of negation; so it is as though He said "and he does not make clear in disputation". Like it is the case in al-Kitāb [of Sībawayh]: أَنَا زَيْدًا غَيْرُ ضَارِبٍ ("I am not one to strike Zayd"). It is also said: [زَيْدًا] is accusative by a verb that ضَارِبٍ explains, and likewise in the verse.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدَى مِمَّا وَجَدْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَكُمْ قَالُوا إِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ (٢٤)).
His saying (قُلْ أَوَلَوْ): in the form of the imperative, and it is resumptive. It is also read (قَالَ), meaning the warner mentioned [before].

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ (٢٦)).
His saying (بَرَاءٌ): with fatḥa on the bāʾ and a single hamza; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of the active participle, in the sense of بَرِيءٌ ("free of"), and that has also been read.

ukberi-tibyan:3-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (٣) وَإِنَّهُ فِي أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ (٤) أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكُمُ الذِّكْرَ صَفْحًا أَنْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا مُسْرِفِينَ (٥))
His saying (فِي أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to عَلِيٌّ, and the lām does not prevent that.
And (لَدَيْنَا) is a badal (substitute) of the preposition and its genitive noun. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْكِتَابِ, or of «أُمِّ». Neither of the two adverbial phrases can be the khabar (predicate), because the khabar must be «عَلِيٌّ» on account of the lām; but each of them may be a naʿt (adjective) of the khabar, which became a ḥāl by being placed before it.
And (صَفْحًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of نَضْرِبُ, because it has the sense of نَصْفَحُ ("We turn aside"); it may also be a ḥāl.
It was also read with ḍamma on the ṣād (صُفْحًا), and the more likely view is that it is a dialectal variant. And (أَنْ), with fatḥa on the hamza, means "because you were" (لِأَنْ كُنْتُمْ); and with kasra on it (إِنْ) it is conditional, and what precedes indicates the apodosis.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ (٣١)).
His saying (عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ): i.e. from one of the two towns, Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif. It is also said: the implied wording is "upon one man of two men from the two towns".
It is also said: the man was one who lived in Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif and went back and forth between them, so he became as though he were one of the people of both.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْلَا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنَا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفًا مِنْ فَضَّةٍ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ (٣٣)).
His saying (لِبُيُوتِهِمْ): it is a badal (substitute) with the preposition repeated, i.e. "for the houses of whoever disbelieved".
السَّقْفُ (roof) is a singular with a plural meaning; and سُقُفًا, with ḍamma, is a plural, like رَهْنٌ and رُهُنٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَنَا قَالَ يَا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ الْقَرِينُ (٣٨)).
His saying (جَاءَنَا): in the singular, referring back to the wording of مَنْ; and in the dual (جَاءَانَا), referring back to the two towns [Translator's note: the text has «الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ» ("the two towns"), evidently for «الْقَرِينَيْنِ» ("the two companions"), as the following words show]: the disbeliever and his devil. And (الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ): it is said that He meant the east and the west, giving one the dominant role (taghlīb), as in الْقَمَرَيْنِ ("the two moons", i.e. the sun and the moon).

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ إِذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي الْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ (٣٩)).
His saying (وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ): there are two views on the fāʿil (agent). The first: «أَنَّكُمْ» and what it governs, i.e. "your consoling one another in the punishment will not benefit you".
The second: that it is the pronoun of the wishing (al-tamannī) indicated by His saying (يَالَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ), i.e. "wishing for distance will not benefit you"; on this view «أَنَّكُمْ» means "because you…" (لِأَنَّكُمْ).
As for (إِذْ), its matter is problematic, because it is an adverb of past time, whereas لَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمْ, its agent, and the day mentioned are not past.
Ibn Jinnī said, in his questioning of Abū ʿAlī: "I went back to him about it many times, and the last thing I obtained from him was that this world and the next are connected, and they are the same in the judgement and knowledge of Allah the Exalted; so «إِذْ» is a badal (substitute) of الْيَوْمَ, so that it is as though it were future, or as though the day were past." Another said: the speech is construed according to the meaning, and the meaning is that the establishment of their wrongdoing in their own eyes will take place on the Day of Resurrection; so it is as though He said "it will not benefit you today, when your wrongdoing has been confirmed to you"; so it is also a badal.
Others said: the implied wording is "after you did wrong" (بَعْدَ إِذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ), and the muḍāf was omitted because it is understood.
It is also said: إِذْ has the sense of أَنْ, i.e. "because you did wrong". It is also read «إِنَّكُمْ فِي الْعَذَابِ», with kasra on the hamza, as resumptive; and this is on the view that the agent is the wishing.
On this view it is also possible that the agent is "your wrongdoing" or "your denial", indicated by ظَلَمْتُمْ; and the agent omitted from the wording is then what governs إِذْ, not the pronoun of the agent.

ukberi-tibyan:52-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْ هَذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ (٥٢) فَلَوْلَا أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ (٥٣)).
His saying (أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ): «أَمْ» here is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) in wording, because a clause occurs after it; but in meaning it is connected and correlative (muttaṣila muʿādila), since the meaning is "Am I better than him or not?", or "Which of us is better?".
And (أَسْوِرَةٌ) is the plural of سِوَارٌ (bracelet). As for أَسَاوِرَةٌ, it is the plural of إِسْوَارٌ, or the plural of أَسْوِرَةٌ, a plural of a plural; its original form is أَسَاوِيرُ, and the yāʾ was made a compensation for the tāʾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the usual statement is that the tāʾ of أَسَاوِرَةٌ compensates for the yāʾ of أَسَاوِيرُ].

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفًا وَمَثَلًا لِلْآخِرِينَ (٥٦)).
As for «سَلَفًا», it is a singular with a plural meaning, like النَّاسُ and الرَّهْطُ.
As for سُلُفًا, with two ḍammas, it is a plural like أَسَدٌ and أُسُدٌ; or the plural of سَالِفٌ, like صَابِرٌ and صُبُرٌ; or the plural of سَلِيفٌ, like رَغِيفٌ and رُغُفٌ. As for سُلَفًا, with ḍamma on the sīn and fatḥa on the lām, it is said: the ḍamma was replaced with a fatḥa for lightness.
It is also said: it is the plural of سُلْفَةٌ, like غُرْفَةٌ and غُرَفٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ (٥٧)).
His saying (مَثَلًا): it is the second object of ضُرِبَ, i.e. "he was made an example". It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. he was mentioned as one used for comparison. And (يَصِدُّونَ), with ḍamma on the ṣād (يَصُدُّونَ), means "they turn away"; and with kasra on it, it is a dialectal variant of it.
It is also said: [the form with] kasra means "they clamour".

ukberi-tibyan:6-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَمْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ نَبِيٍّ فِي الْأَوَّلِينَ (٦) وَمَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (٧) فَأَهْلَكْنَا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشًا وَمَضَى مَثَلُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (٨)).
(وَكَمْ) is accusative by «أَرْسَلْنَا», and (بَطْشًا) is a tamyīz (specification). It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent, i.e. "We destroyed them, [We] being violent in assault" (أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بَاطِشِينَ).

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ نَشَاءُ لَجَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ مَلَائِكَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ (٦٠)).
His saying (لَجَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ): i.e. "in place of you".
It is also said: the meaning is "We would have turned some of you into angels".

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (٦٦)).
His saying {أَن تأتيهم}: it is a badal (substitute) of السَّاعَةَ — a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: {يُطَاف عَلَيْهِم بصحاف من ذهب وأكواب}
His saying (يُطَافُ): the implied wording of the speech is "they enter, and then [the vessels] are passed around"; it was omitted because the meaning is understood.

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ (٧٥)).
His saying (لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a second khabar (predicate); and both are tawkīd (emphasis).

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَادَوْا يَا مَالِكُ لْيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ مَاكِثُونَ (٧٧)).
His saying (يَامَالِكُ): it is read «يَا مَالِ», with kasra and with ḍamma, by way of vocative truncation (tarkhīm).

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنْ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعَابِدِينَ (٨١)).
His saying (إِنْ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدٌ): «إِنْ» has the sense of «مَا» (negation).
It is also said: it is conditional, i.e. "if you say that, then I am the first to affirm His oneness".
It is also said: "if that were true, I would be the first of those who disdain to worship him" — and that will never be true.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي السَّمَاءِ إِلَهٌ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَهٌ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ (٨٤)).
His saying (وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي السَّمَاءِ إِلَهٌ): the ṣila (relative clause) of «الَّذِي» can only be a clause, and the implied wording here is "and He is the One who is God in the heaven". «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to إِلَهٌ, i.e. "worshipped in the heaven and worshipped in the earth". It is not sound to make «إِلَهٌ» a mubtadaʾ (subject) and فِي السَّمَاءِ its khabar (predicate), because then no referring pronoun would remain for الَّذِي; it would be like your saying هُوَ الَّذِي فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدٌ ("He is the one who — in the house is Zayd"). The same holds if you make إِلَهٌ nominative by the adverbial phrase. If you place in the adverbial phrase a pronoun referring to الَّذِي and make إِلَهٌ a badal (substitute) of it, that is permissible, though weak, because the overall purpose is to affirm His divinity, not His being in the heavens and the earth. It would also be unsound from another angle, namely His saying «وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَهٌ»: for it is conjoined to what precedes it, and if you do not assume what we have mentioned, it becomes cut off from it, and the meaning would be "in the earth there is a god".

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقِيلِهِ يَا رَبِّ إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَوْمٌ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٨٨)).
His saying (وَقِيلِهِ): in the accusative (وَقِيلَهُ), and there are several views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «سِرَّهُمْ», i.e. "He knows their secret and his saying".
The second: that it is conjoined to the position of السَّاعَةِ, i.e. "and with Him is [the knowledge] that He knows the Hour, and his saying". The third: that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and he said his saying".
It is also read in the nominative (وَقِيلُهُ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «يَا رَبِّ» as its khabar (predicate). It is also said: the implied wording is "and his saying is the saying 'O Lord'". It is also said: the khabar is omitted, i.e. "his saying 'O Lord' is heard", or "is answered".
It was also read in the genitive (وَقِيلِهِ), conjoined to the wording of السَّاعَةِ. It is also said: it is an oath. And Allah knows best.
